about: Every uncertifiable finding is a falsifiable claim: it says the evidence that would
settle the question is not here. A case states the obligation, then either the ways it
can be discharged -- the evidence, and what the checker must say once it is present --
or a written reason why no evidence can. scripts/obligation-audit.mjs enforces both.
Snippets run against the audited published typings, not fixture stubs, for the reason
AGENTS.md gives: an obligation that only exists against a loosened stub is not an

cases.why: Whether props.title is a reactive getter or a plain property is decided by the component's callers, and an exported component may be rendered by code this build cannot see.

closes.evidence: a visible caller passes a signal, and no unseen caller can unwrite that call site
the caller set is complete because the component is local, and every caller passes a static value
the user asserts the analyzed files are the whole program, so the export reaches no unseen caller

cases.why: Destructuring props unwraps each property once, which is a defect only if the property is reactive -- and that is the caller's fact.

closes.evidence: a visible caller passes a signal

cases.why: An exported helper that creates an effect may be called with or without an owner, and its callers cannot be enumerated.

closes.evidence: the helper is local, so its sole call site inside createRoot is the whole caller set
the user asserts a closed program, so the enumerated call sites decide the owner
the sole call site is at module scope, where no owner can be live

cases.why: A getter's body runs on access, so no value written in the literal proves what the property yields; the graph cannot be certified JSON-safe.

closes.evidence: the property is a plain data property holding a Date, so JSON.stringify provably flattens it
every property is a data property with a JSON-safe leaf, in a literal closed against spreads and computed keys

cases.why: A broad `number` may be NaN or Infinity, and JSON cannot carry either faithfully.
cases.irreducible: No source fact narrows a declared `number` to the finite subset. A finite *literal* is a different value with its own constant fact, and the compiler's numeric domain is already consulted: an all-finite-constituents guarantee certifies, and its absence is the obligation. Nothing else about the program can decide it.

closes.evidence: the declared domain is a finite literal union, so every inhabitant is JSON-safe

cases.why: Solid 1.x does not treat a direct JSX return as component identity: an exported function returning JSX may instead be used as a tracked render callback, whose body *is* a tracking scope. Until a caller settles which, the read's execution model is unknown.

closes.evidence: an exact JSX call site proves the function is rendered as a component, so its body runs once and untracked

cases.why: Both primitives gate the write on !response.committed, and createSSRResponse commits at the shell flush. Content below a Loading boundary may settle on either side of that flush.
cases.irreducible: Whether the boundary settles before or after the shell flush is decided per request, by how long the awaited work takes. It is not a property of the program, so no fact about the source can decide it. Selecting a client-only rendering mode removes the subject entirely rather than deciding the timing, and that is a different case.
